name: 5x5 percentage scheme

card.summary: The 5x5 percentage scheme is a strength-training plan of five sets of five reps at a set percentage of a lifter's one-rep max, used to build strength and muscle that shape the physique.

quick.overview:
This scheme prescribes five sets of five repetitions at a fixed percentage of the lifter's one-repetition maximum (1RM). It is a way of structuring heavy compound lifts.

Training at 80 to 100% of 1RM for 1 to 5 reps is the usual range for building strength, and muscle growth follows from progressive overload and total volume, which is how people use it to build a more muscular physique.
quick.how: Lifters estimate their 1RM, set working weights as percentages of it, and raise the numbers over weeks. Forum logs show people combining it with programmes such as 5/3/1 and Sheiko-style plans.
quick.risks: Typical risks of heavy lifting apply: joint and muscle strain from poor form or excess load. Forum users also report difficulty hitting prescribed percentages on some lifts.

lead: The 5x5 percentage scheme sets five sets of five reps at a percentage of one-repetition maximum. Percent-based loading is a common way to manage intensity in strength training.[1]

Wikipedia describes 1 to 5 reps at roughly 80 to 100% of 1RM as the strength range, and notes that training volume has a positive relationship with hypertrophy.[1] Muscle growth and strength are the main effects of resistance training.[1]

angle.text: The scheme is a loading structure for compound lifts. People use it to build muscle mass, which changes body shape.

paras: Load is set as a percentage of a tested or estimated 1RM, and weights are progressively increased over time.[1] Training logs on T Nation show lifters mixing 5x5 work with 5/3/1 templates and other programmes.[2][3]
No studies found specific to this scheme. General research on set, rep and load ranges is summarised under strength training.[1]
